definitions.explanation: A channel or ditch running alongside a road or building to carry away rainwater and wastewater.

examples.japanese: {側溝|そっこう}に{落|お}ち{葉|ば}が{詰|つ}まっている。
examples.english: The drainage ditch is clogged with fallen leaves.

examples.japanese: {大雨|おおあめ}のとき、{側溝|そっこう}から{水|みず}があふれた。
examples.english: During the heavy rain, water overflowed from the roadside gutter.

examples.japanese: {自転車|じてんしゃ}の{前輪|ぜんりん}が{側溝|そっこう}の{蓋|ふた}の{隙間|すきま}に{挟|はさ}まって{転倒|てんとう}しそうになった。
examples.english: The front wheel of my bicycle got caught in the gap of a gutter cover and I nearly fell over.

notes:
A compound of {側|そく} (side) and {溝|こう} (ditch, channel). Refers to the concrete or stone channels that run along the edges of roads in Japan to drain rainwater.

In Japanese residential areas, {側溝|そっこう} are ubiquitous — nearly every street has them. They are often covered with metal or concrete grates. Bicycle riders in Japan learn to be careful of {側溝|そっこう} grates, as thin tires can get caught in the gaps.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {側溝|そっこう}の{蓋|ふた}: gutter cover, drain cover
- {側溝|そっこう}の{掃除|そうじ}: gutter cleaning
- {側溝|そっこう}に{落|お}ちる: to fall into a ditch
- {側溝|そっこう}が{詰|つ}まる: for a gutter to become clogged

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {排水溝|はいすいこう}: drain, drainage channel — more general term for any drainage outlet
- {溝|みぞ}: ditch, groove — everyday word for any channel or groove
- {用水路|ようすいろ}: irrigation channel — carries water for agricultural use
